Hey, I'm Igor 👋

Founder & engineer at RioBlocks · Lead Engineer at MemPalace · Blockchain infrastructure at EOS Rio

I build developer tools, AI infrastructure, and low-level systems. My work spans data engines, networking, applications for working with AI agents, and blockchain infrastructure.

I work across TypeScript, Rust, Zig, and Python, choosing the tools that fit the problem.

This card is powered by MyRank.dev, a developer profiles and rankings platform I built.

Things I build

  • MyRank.dev — Developer profiles and rankings built from verified commit history.
  • AfterPic — AI-powered photo editor.
  • WormDB — An embeddable key-value engine in Zig, with write-once records, native stored procedures, and vector search.
  • Agent Portal — A desktop app for browsing and migrating sessions between coding agents, built with Rust, Tauri, and Angular.
  • ShellPort — A browser-based remote terminal in a single binary, with its own Canvas2D terminal emulator.
  • Meshrooms — Shared rooms for people and their agents, bringing conversations, tasks, files, and decisions together. Currently in beta.

Developer tools & libraries

  • meshguard — A peer-to-peer, WireGuard-compatible mesh VPN daemon in Zig, with no central coordinator.
  • context-builder — A Rust CLI for assembling codebase context for LLM prompts.
  • universal-llm-client — A TypeScript client for working with multiple LLM providers through one interface.
  • comfyui-node — A fully typed Node.js client for programmatic ComfyUI control.
  • Angular Translation Service — Signal-based i18n with runtime language switching, SSR support, and a companion CLI.
  • FontAwesome MCP — An independent MCP server for finding icons and retrieving SVGs and integration guidance.

MemPalace

I'm the lead developer and a project maintainer at MemPalace, an open-source AI memory system.

My work spans core development, ingestion reliability, data preservation, retrieval quality, performance, and security, alongside reviewing contributions and maintaining the codebase.

Open-source contributions

  • llmman (formerly inferrs) — My contributions during the inferrs era include Ollama API compatibility for thinking mode and duration metrics, plus a CUDA static-linking fix.

I've also contributed upstream fixes to uWebSockets.js, Engine.IO, Angular Font Awesome, and Abieos.

Blockchain infrastructure at EOS Rio

Over the years, I've worked on infrastructure and tooling for Antelope-based blockchains with the EOS Rio team.

  • Hyperion — Full-history API and indexer, alongside its explorer and streaming client.
  • fleet-router — A Rust reverse proxy and load balancer for Antelope SHiP, with range-aware routing and failover.
  • hyperion-tools — Rust tooling for state-history decoding, snapshot ingestion, and log recovery, including experimental components.
  • SimplEOS — A desktop wallet for the Antelope ecosystem.
  • node-abieos and rs-abieos — Node.js and Rust bindings for Abieos.
  • bp-info-standard — A standard for block producer metadata.

RioBlocks · EOS Rio · MyRank · AfterPic

Hi, I'm Sam 👋

Android & iOS Developer 📱 · Web Developer 🌐 · Hackathon Enjoyer 🏆

Bahamut is the new home of the FINAL FANTASY XIV 1.23b development I am working on moving forward.
If you'd like to participate as a developer or tester, or try our hosted server, join our Discord.

👨‍💻 About me

I'm a mobile developer who builds for Android (Kotlin) and iOS (Swift) by day, and dabbles in just about everything else by night — Rust, C/C++, TypeScript, and a healthy collection of emulators, game engines, and CLI tools. I love shipping things, learning new stacks, and the occasional weekend hackathon.

When I'm not writing apps, I'm usually reverse-engineering and reviving an old game I love. ⚔️

🐉 Final Fantasy XIV hobby projects

A big chunk of my free time goes toward preserving FINAL FANTASY XIV v1.23b — the original 2010 1.0 release, before A Realm Reborn. It's a piece of MMO history that the world otherwise lost, and bringing it back to life is my favorite playground.

  • ⚙️ Garlemald-Server — A Rust port of Project Meteor Server: a private-server emulator for FFXIV 1.0. Lobby, world, map, and web services in a single Cargo workspace, backed by SQLite and driving 1,142 upstream Lua content scripts.
  • 🚀 Garlemald-Client — A cross-platform Rust launcher for FFXIV v1.23b private servers (macOS / Linux / Windows).
  • 🔬 meteor-decomp & decomp-agents — Decompilation tooling for digging into the original client.
  • 🍎 XIV-1.0-Apple-Silicon-Installer — Getting the 1.0 client running on Apple Silicon.
  • 🐧 XIV-1.0-Linux-Installer — Getting the 1.0 client running on x86_64 Linux, across distributions.

🌐 It all lives at garlemaldsoftware.com — docs, idiot-proof quick-start guides, and downloads for every project in one place.

🛠️ Tech I work with

🤝 Find & follow great developers

This profile takes some inspiration from yumiaura and her followme project — a tool that discovers GitHub repositories, grades them with a local Ollama model, then follows promising authors and stars strong projects. It's a great reminder that the best part of GitHub is the people. If you're building something cool, say hi — I'm always happy to follow along. ⭐

📊 Stats

Thanks for stopping by — and if you make it back to Eorzea, I'll see you in 1.0. ✨

Hi, I'm Anton 👋

Embedded & IoT engineer — energy metering · CAN bus · reverse engineering · ESPHome

I build firmware and tools that live at the boundary between hardware and software: reading electricity & water meters, sniffing automotive CAN buses, and reverse-engineering embedded devices. Most of my open work ships as ESPHome components for utility meters, plus the protocol libraries underneath them. When I'm not on a serial bus, I'm designing PCBs in KiCad.

⭐ Highlights

jeep-canbus 30 CAN bus projects for Chrysler/Jeep — VES enabler and other hacks.
painlessMeshMqttGateway 27 MQTT ↔ painlessMesh gateway bridging an IoT mesh to Ethernet.

🧩 ESPHome — Core Contributions

I'm an active contributor to the official ESPHome project, where I've authored and maintain a number of sensor, display, and accelerometer components that now ship with ESPHome itself. (merged PRs · all PRs)

…plus fixes & enhancements to LTR390, INA226, VEML7700, BME280, the ac_dimmer (ESP-IDF 5+), and the i2c bus.

I'm also one of the main developers of esphome-libs/dlms_parser — the shared DLMS/COSEM parsing library used across the ESPHome ecosystem, which grew out of my own esphome-dlms-cosem work.

In progress (open PRs): AS7341 / AS7343 spectral sensors, HUSB238 USB-PD controller, ST LIS2DH12 & LIS2DW12 accelerometers, Waveshare CH32V003 I/O expander, CST328 touch controller, BH1745 colour sensor, and signal filters.
